title: A counterexample to Liu's conjecture on Fano indices in dimension four: paper, Lean 4 formalization and verification code
description:
H. Liu (arXiv:2608.03434, Conjecture 4.2) conjectured that, in each dimension n >= 2, the Fano indices of canonical weighted projective n-spaces (together with 1, ..., n), the indices of terminal Calabi-Yau n-folds and the indices of n-dimensional log canonical singularities form the same set. The paper shows that 1389 is the index of a terminal Calabi-Yau fourfold and of a four-dimensional log canonical singularity that is not klt, both built from a symmetry of order 1389 of the hypersurface x0^77 x1 + x1^67 x2 + x2^7 x0 + x3^3 + x4^2 = 0 in P(1,1,11,26,39), and that 1389 is not the Fano index of any canonical weighted projective fourspace. So the conjecture fails in dimension four.

paper/ holds the LaTeX source (amsart) and the compiled PDF; dist/ holds the PDF, an anonymized PDF for double-anonymous review, the LaTeX source zip, the arXiv tarball and MasterLiuIndexConjectureZip.zip with every file of the repository. lean/ is a Lean 4 and Mathlib project proving 1389 notin I_{4,wps}, with Kasprzyk's criterion as the definition of canonical, through a certificate of 4,022 units checked by decide +kernel, and the algebraic lemmas on the hypersurface; its theorems depend only on the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. code/ contains exhaustive searches over all 1,301,769,806 partitions of 1389 into five parts in C, C++, Julia and Python, and scripts/run_all.sh regenerates the certificate, builds the Lean project, checks the axioms and runs all searches.
